description: rangeStrategy: always bump dependencies, even when the new version is already in the range.
rebaseWhen: rebase only on conflicts, to save unnecessary workflow runs.
internalChecksFilter: hold updates that do not yet satisfy minimumReleaseAge instead of raising a pending PR, which would run CI and fail pnpm's minimumReleaseAge policy.
ignoreDeps: ubuntu must be the oldest possible version, for binary compatibility with older operating systems.

customDatasources and the packageRules that use them: the libraries and tools that Freelens also has take the version Freelens has on main, not the newest release. See the packageRules for which ones. The custom datasources return one release, the version Freelens has, so those rules replace the current value rather than bump it: bump looks for the current version among the releases and skips a dependency with no lock file that it cannot find there.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes must not be delayed by minimumReleaseAge.

description: mise.lock pins a checksum and a URL per tool per platform, but a local `mise install` re-locks only the platform it runs on and silently leaves the other seven stale.
Lock file maintenance runs plain `mise lock`, which refreshes every tool on every platform already in the file.

Defaults are disabled and weekly, hence the explicit settings. The packageRules keep it to mise.lock, since pnpm-lock.yaml is updated with each dependency update and does not want a periodic refresh PR.

packageRules.description: No lock file maintenance by default: pnpm-lock.yaml is updated with each dependency update.
Lock file maintenance for mise.lock only.

Delay npm updates until they satisfy pnpm's minimumReleaseAge policy (1 day by default since pnpm v11). Only npm packages land in pnpm-lock.yaml, so this is scoped to the npm datasource and leaves the other datasources untouched.
No delay for @freelensapp/extensions, which pnpm-workspace.yaml excludes from minimumReleaseAge.

description: Libraries that Freelens also has take the version of its default catalog in pnpm-workspace.yaml on main: the extension compiles and tests against the versions the host runs.

Every dependency except the ones excluded with ! here: a dependency added to package.json is in the Freelens catalog unless it is added to that list. One that is in neither fails its lookup on the Dependency Dashboard.
js-base64 and moment are bundled libraries that Freelens does not have, so they are updated from the npm registry as usual.
The custom datasource has no release dates, so minimumReleaseAge is off; Freelens has the same pnpm policy and adopts only versions that already satisfy it.

packageRules.description: pnpm and the mise of the workflows are updated from their own registries, not to the versions of Freelens, but in the Freelens group pull request, so that one pull request carries every toolchain update.

Tools run with pnpm dlx, and the Biome and Prettier that Trunk runs, take the version Freelens runs with pnpm dlx in the scripts of its root package.json on main, except the ones excluded with ! here, which Freelens does not run. The custom datasource has no release dates, so minimumReleaseAge is off.

The tools in mise.toml and Node in .nvmrc take the versions in mise.toml of Freelens on main, where Node is the version bundled in Electron. The mise manager expects a leading v in the releases of tools that come from GitHub, which mise.toml does not have, so extractVersion makes it optional. The custom datasource has no release dates, so minimumReleaseAge is off.
The Node runtime of Trunk takes the version in mise.toml of Freelens on main, like the one in mise.toml here. The custom datasource has no release dates, so minimumReleaseAge is off.
No updates of engines.node, the oldest Node the extension runs on, which Freelens keeps as a range too. engines.freelens is updated by the custom manager for it.
Group @freelensapp/* with everything that follows Freelens into one PR, so that a nightly of @freelensapp/extensions and the stack it was built with arrive together.

description: peerDependencies are not bumped by vulnerability fixes either.

Renovate turns every vulnerability alert into a package rule appended after these ones, with the vulnerabilityAlerts settings in its force object. Forced settings override every other rule, so vulnerabilityAlerts.rangeStrategy replaces the widen strategy above, and no package rule can put it back.

Package rules are applied again to each update after the lookup, when the update already carries isVulnerabilityAlert. This rule drops the peer range change from the fix at that point, while the other dependencies in the same fix keep the bump strategy.

freelens-catalog.description: The version of a library in the default catalog of Freelens on main.

freelens-dlx.description: The version of a tool that a script in the root package.json of Freelens on main runs with pnpm dlx: the text after `dlx <name>@` up to the next space or the end of the script.

freelens-mise.description: The version of a tool in mise.toml of Freelens on main.

customManagers.description: The freelens engine field in package.json.
Renovate hints in a comment after the version.
